title: Personal and Work Accounts
body: Personal and Work Accounts On supported AI sites, the Whiteout browser extension notes which kind of account each prompt was sent from: a personal account, your organization's workspace, or no account at all. Desktop Guard does the same in desktop AI apps that show the account on screen. A prompt sent from a personal ChatGPT or Claude account falls under that vendor's consumer terms, not your organization's contract, even when your policies allowed the prompt itself. To allow or block by account, set an account rule on the AI app, for example "work accounts only" for ChatGPT. This page explains how the account is read and what each value means. This needs browser extension 1.14.0 or later. --- Where it shows Where What you see --- --- Governance → Prompt Review An Account column on each prompt Activity → AI Activity A Personal accounts column per tool: the share of that tool's prompts sent from personal accounts, out of the prompts whose account type is known. — means no account type was seen. Coverage → AI Footprint Chips on Web AI rows, such as 4 personal · 9 unknown . These count people, not prompts, over the last 30 days. Someone who used two kinds of account is counted in both. This is the account on the AI site . It's different from the Account column under Coverage → Enrollment → Browsers , which is the account signed in to the browser profile. See Browser coverage. AI apps people connected through your identity provider, and AI use from a vendor's audit log, count as work accounts, because they went through your organization's own tenant. See AI apps connected with work accounts. What the values mean Value Meaning --- --- Personal account , or Personal (Plus) with the plan A personal account or a personal plan on the AI site Work workspace , for example Work workspace (Enterprise) A business plan, signed in with one of your organization's email domains Work email, unverified workspace Signed in with one of your organization's email domains, but Whiteout couldn't confirm the workspace belongs to your organization Signed out Sent without signing in to the AI site Unknown account , or Unknown account (Team) with the plan The site was used, but Whiteout couldn't tell whose account it was Not observable This surface can't see the account: IDEs, desktop apps that don't show it, older extensions and sites not listed below. It never means a work account. A personal plan wins over a work email. Someone who signed up for ChatGPT Plus with their work address is counted as personal. The plan decides which terms cover the data, not the mailbox used to sign up. --- How each site is read Site How Whiteout tells What you'll see --- --- --- Claude The plan of the signed-in Claude organization, read from claude.ai with the page's own session (as the Claude page itself does), or else the plan label in Claude's sidebar Free, Pro or Max: Personal . Team or Enterprise: Unknown account (Team) or (Enterprise) , because claude.ai doesn't show the account's email domain. ChatGPT The plan shown in ChatGPT's own interface: the label in the profile menu or sidebar, an Upgrade plan button (Free), or a workspace switcher. Whiteout never reads ChatGPT's session data. Free, Plus, Pro or Go: Personal . Team, Business, Enterprise or Edu: Unknown account with the plan, because ChatGPT doesn't show the account's email domain. Guest chats: Signed out . Gemini The domain of the Google account shown on Gemini's account button. Only the domain is read. gmail.com or another personal email provider: Personal . One of your organization's domains: Work email, unverified workspace . Any other domain: Unknown account . Not signed in: Signed out . Microsoft Copilot (copilot.com, where copilot.microsoft.com now redirects) The site itself. Both work and personal Microsoft accounts sign in there, so the site doesn't say which. Unknown account Microsoft 365 Copilot (cloud.microsoft and the Microsoft 365 Copilot app) The site itself: it accepts work accounts only, but it doesn't show which organization Unknown account Perplexity An Enterprise badge in Perplexity's interface Unknown account (Enterprise) when the badge shows. Otherwise the account type can't be read. DeepSeek DeepSeek has no organization accounts Always Personal Any other site Not read Not observable Reading copilot.com as Unknown account needs browser extension 1.16.0 or later. If copilot.microsoft.com itself loads without redirecting, it still reads as Personal or Signed out , as before. Work workspace needs a business plan and one of your organization's email domains together. None of the sites above shows both today, so Work workspace doesn't appear for them yet. Your organization's domains are the domain set up for your organization in Whiteout, any additional email domains registered for it, and the domain of a Google Workspace identity provider. --- Privacy Never the email address. For Gemini, only the domain part is read on the page. For the other sites, no email address is read at all. Never tokens or session data. Whiteout never reads the AI vendor's passwords, cookies, access tokens or session data. ChatGPT's session data carries an access token, so the extension reads only what ChatGPT shows on screen. A one-way fingerprint, not an identity. Whiteout stores a one-way fingerprint of the vendor account, mixed with your organization's ID, so repeat use of the same account can be recognized without storing who it is. Never delays a prompt. The account type is read when the page loads. If it can't be read, the prompt goes as normal and shows Not observable . SOC events include the account type and plan, never the fingerprint. --- What isn't built yet Most desktop apps and all IDEs. Desktop Guard reads the account only where a desktop app shows it on screen, and which apps it can read is still expanding. Prompts from coding agents show Not observable .
